He played [[college basketball]] for the [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA Bruins]], where he earned first-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|all-conference]] honors in the Pac-10 (known now as the [[Pac-12]]) as a sophomore in 2011. Honeycutt was selected by the [[Sacramento Kings]] in the second round of the [[2011 NBA draft]]. He played with the Kings for two seasons and in 2013 moved to Europe, where he played for [[EuroLeague]] clubs [[BC Khimki|Khimki]] and [[Anadolu Efes S.K.|Anadolu Efes]]. He committed suicide at age 27 following a shootout with police. ==High school career== Honeycutt attended [[Sylmar High School]] in [[Sylmar, California]]. Considered a four-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Honeycutt was listed as the No. 4 [[small forward]] and the No. 28 player in the nation in 2009.{{cite web |title=Rivals.com |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Tyler-Honeycutt-83475;_ylt=An9LxMM3tuivrdyoN4D3COtGPZB4 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20150130011357/http://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Tyler-Honeycutt-83475;_ylt=An9LxMM3tuivrdyoN4D3COtGPZB4 |archive-date=January 30, 2015 |url-status=dead|website=sports.yahoo.com}} ==College career== [[File:Arizona vs UCLA 2011.jpg|thumb|Honeycutt (front right) in a game against [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]] in 2011]] In his freshman year at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] (UCLA) in [[2009–10 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2009–10]], Honeycutt played in the final 26 games, starting 18, and led the team in [[rebound (basketball)|rebounding]] at 6.5 per game. He was named to the [[Pac-10]] All-Freshman team.{{cite web |title=Player Bio: Tyler Honeycutt |url=https://uclabruins.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/tyler-honeycutt/2380 |access-date=June 5, 2023 |work=uclabruins.com}} In [[2010–11 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|the following season]], he was named the team's co-MVP (with [[Malcolm Lee (basketball)|Malcolm Lee]] and [[Reeves Nelson]]) and first-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-10]] after averaging 12.8 points per game and leading the conference in [[block (basketball)|blocks]] with 2.1 per game.{{cite news |last=Maya |first=Adam |date=April 12, 2011 |title=UCLA basketball: Lee, Honeycutt, Nelson MVPs |newspaper=Orange County Register |url=http://ucla.ocregister.com/2011/04/12/ucla-basketball-lee-honeycutt-nelson-team-mvps/31613/ |url-status=dead |access-date=December 4, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120323114610/http://ucla.ocregister.com/2011/04/12/ucla-basketball-lee-honeycutt-nelson-team-mvps/31613/ |archive-date=March 23, 2012}} He [[NBA draft declaration|declared for the NBA draft]] after the season.{{cite news |last=Brennan |first=Eamonn |title=Final exam: Grading the goners |date=April 25, 2011 |work=ESPN.com |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/news/story?id=6425414 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110427163630/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/news/story?id=6425414 |url-status=live |archive-date=April 27, 2011}} Honeycutt was projected as a late [[NBA draft lottery|lottery]] pick to mid-first-round pick in the [[2011 NBA draft]] but concerns over inconsistency and less-than-maximum effort dropped him to the second round. The [[Sacramento Kings]] took him with the 35th overall pick.{{cite web |last=Bolch |first=Ben |title=Two former UCLA basketball stars die tragically, leaving questions behind |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/la-sp-ucla-honeycutt-knight-20180814-story.html |website=Los Angeles Times |access-date=June 28, 2021 |date=August 15, 2018}} ==Professional career== ===Sacramento Kings (2011–2013)=== Honeycutt was drafted in the second round with the 35th overall pick by the [[Sacramento Kings]] in the [[2011 NBA draft]].{{cite news |last=Maya |first=Adam |title=What were UCLA's Honeycutt, Lee thinking? |date=June 24, 2011 |newspaper= The Orange County Register |url=http://www.ocregister.com/sports/honeycutt-305837-lee-point.html game on December 31, 2011, and scored two points in four minutes.{{cite news |last=Ham |first=James |title=Notebook: Knicks 114, Kings 92 |date=December 31, 2011 |work=NBA.com [[Houston Rockets]] along with [[Thomas Robinson (basketball)|Thomas Robinson]] and [[Francisco García (basketball)|Francisco García]] in exchange for [[Patrick Patterson (basketball)|Patrick Patterson]], [[Toney Douglas]] and [[Cole Aldrich]].{{cite news |last=Shanks |first=Chad |date=February 20, 2013 |title=Rockets Acquire Robinson, Garcia and Honeycutt |work=NBA.com was [[Waivers (NBA)|waived]] by the Rockets on March 5, so they could sign guard [[Aaron Brooks (basketball)|Aaron Brooks]].{{cite web |last=Suarez |first=P. |date=March 5, 2013 |title=He's Back - Honeycutt and Mitchell Watt |url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/israel/61715/ironi-nes-ziona-announced-tyler-honeycutt-and-mitchell-watt.html |url-status=dead |access-date=August 18, 2013 On July 8, 2014, he signed a two-year deal with the Russian team [[BC Khimki|Khimki]].{{cite news|title=Khimki lands Honeycutt|url=http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/138519|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140713070444/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/138519|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 13, 2014|access-date=July 8, 2014|work=Eurocupbasketball.com|date=July 8, 2014}} In 2014–15 season, he won the [[2014–15 Eurocup Basketball|Eurocup]] championship with Khimki, Europe's second-tier competition. In [[2015–16 Euroleague]], he made his debut in Europe's top competition. Over 23 EuroLeague games, he averaged 6 points and 6.1 rebounds per game. === Anadolu Efes (2016–2017) === On July 22, 2016, Honeycutt signed a 1+1 deal with Turkish club [[Anadolu Efes S.K.|Anadolu Efes]],{{cite news |date=July 22, 2016 |title=Anadolu Efes lands athletic forward Honeycutt |work=Euroleague.net |url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/75cwued5j6v5iix3 |url-status=dead |access-date=July 22, 2016 |archive-date=July 23, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160723163913/http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/75cwued5j6v5iix3 }} where he won the [[Turkish Basketball Super League]] Slam Dunk Contest. Over 35 EuroLeague games, he averaged career highs of 9.2 points, 7.3 rebounds and 2 assists per game. On June 28, 2017, Efes officially opted out of their deal with Honeycutt, and he became a free agent.{{cite news|title=Anadolu Efes Istanbul part ways with Tyler Honeycutt and DeShaun Thomas|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/238854/anadolu-efes-istanbul-part-ways-with-tyler-honeycutt-and-deshaun-thomas.html|access-date=June 28, 2017|work=Sportando.com|date=June 28, 2017}} === Return to Khimki (2017–2018) === On July 14, 2017, Honeycutt returned to [[Moscow basketball derby|Moscow-based]] Khimki. He signed a contract for the 2017–18 season.{{cite news|title=WELCOME BACK, TYLER!|url=http://en.bckhimki.ru/news/clubnews/2017/july/1216/|access-date=July 14, 2017|work=en.bckhimki.ru|date=July 14, 2017}} After missing the first nine games of the [[2017–18 EuroLeague|EuroLeague season]] due to injury, he returned to the court in late November 2017.{{cite news|last=Gancedo|first=Javier|title=Tyler Honeycutt, Khimki: 'We still have to see our full potential'|date=February 6, 2018|website=Euroleague.net|url=https://admin.euroleague.net/news/interviews/euroleague-2017-18/i/8iq9w5jnx6nw7srp/tyler-honeycutt-khimki-we-still-have-to-see-our-full-potential|access-date=April 7, 2020}}{{cite web|title=Tyler Honeycutt International Stats|work=Basketball Reference|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/international/players/tyler-honeycutt-1.html|access-date=April 7, 2020}} He helped Khimki advance to the [[2018 EuroLeague Playoffs|EuroLeague Playoffs]], where they lost to [[PBC CSKA Moscow|CSKA Moscow]] 3–1 in the quarterfinal series.{{cite web|title=Higgins sends CSKA Moscow back to the Final Four|date=April 27, 2018|website=Eurohoops.net|url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/664663/cska-moscow-back-to-the-final-four/|access-date=April 7, 2020}} Over 17 EuroLeague games, he averaged 9.2 points and 5.4 rebounds per game. In [[2017–18 VTB United League|VTB United League]], Khimki lost the final game to CSKA Moscow, 95–84.{{cite web|title=Domestic leagues roundup: June 10, 2018|date=June 10, 2018|website=EuroleagueBasketball.net|url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/news/i/8spj6peg3vhtsggb/domestic-leagues-roundup-june-10-2018|access-date=April 7, 2020}} ==Death== On the afternoon of July 6, 2018, Honeycutt's mother called [[9-1-1|911]] after he had been acting erratically. She said that he had been using [[nitrous oxide]] "for six months overseas and I think it scrambled his brain."{{cite news|last=Bolch|first=Ben|title=Tyler Honeycutt's mother told police the late UCLA basketball star was 'sucking laughing gas'|date=August 21, 2018|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/la-sp-ucla-tyler-honeycutt-20180821-story.html}}{{cite news |title=Former UCLA star and NBA Player Tyler Honeycutt found dead following shootout with police|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/former-ucla-star-nba-player-tyler-honeycutt-found-dead-following-shootout-police-175759738.html|access-date=July 7, 2018|work=[[Yahoo! Sports]]|date=July 7, 2018}} When police arrived they found that he had barricaded the entrance to his [[Sherman Oaks]] home.{{cite news |title=Tyler Honeycutt kills himself after exchanging gunfire with police|url= https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/24029399|access-date=June 5, 2023 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=July 7, 2018 }}{{cite web |last1=Khan |first1=Amina |last2=Lozano |first2=Carlos |date=July 7, 2018 |title=Former NBA, UCLA player Tyler Honeycutt dead after exchanging gunfire with police in Sherman Oaks |url=https://www.latimes.com/local/lanow/la-me-ln-sherman-oaks-shooting-20180707-story.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20190914131154/https://www.latimes.com/local/lanow/la-me-ln-sherman-oaks-shooting-20180707-story.html |archive-date=September 14, 2019 |website=[[Los Angeles Times]]}} He fired a shot that hit a wall next to an officer, who fired back at Honeycutt. After nine hours, [[LAPD Metropolitan Division#D Platoon (SWAT)|LAPD SWAT]] entered the home early the next morning, and found Honeycutt dead.{{cite news |last=Gleeson |first=Scott |date=8 July 2018 |title=Tyler Honeycutt, former UCLA and Sacramento Kings basketball player, dies after standoff with police |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/basketball/2018/07/07/tyler-honeycutt-ucla-sacramento-kings-police-standoff/765549002/ |work=USA Today |access-date=13 July 2018 }}
{{cite news |last=Downen |first=Robert |date=7 July 2018 |title=Former Rockets player dead after SWAT standoff |url=https://www.chron.com/sports/rockets/article/Former-Rockets-player-dead-after-SWAT-standoff-13056627.php |work=Chronicle |location=Houston |access-date= 13 July 2018 }}
{{cite news |last=Bravo |first=Kristina |date=7 July 2018 |title=Former UCLA Player Dead After Exchanging Gunfire With LAPD in Sherman Oaks, Family Friend Says |url=https://ktla.com/2018/07/07/person-dead-after-police-exchanged-gunfire-with-suspect-in-sherman-oaks-home-lapd/ |work=KTLA |location=Los Angeles |access-date=13 July 2018 }} Bort Escoto, who coached Honeycutt for four years at Sylmar High School, said that "he was a great kid to be around. But he was having some problems", because in Russia he did not know the language and the surroundings, concluding that "he was basically having a hard time with the adjustment. I just kept telling him he needed to get out and meet people". An autopsy determined that he committed [[suicide]] by a gunshot wound to the head.{{cite news|last=Perez|first=A. J. |title=Coroner confirms former NBA, UCLA player Tyler Honeycutt died by suicide|date=July 19, 2018|newspaper=USA Today|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/kings/2018/07/19/death-tyler-honeycutt-ex-ucla-nba-basketball-ruled-suicide/800642002/}} Honeycutt's mother later sued the [[LAPD]], saying it failed to de-escalate the situation and get him medical care.{{Cite web|url=https://abc7.com/5410995/|title=Mother of former UCLA player Tyler Honeycutt suing L.A. for negligence in son's
